Are you ready to celebrate the year's top music videos? Tonight, music's biggest, brightest and most promising artists are gathering at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles for the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards .
From fit checks to performances to culture-shaping confrontations, the VMAs have consistently been the site for some of pop culture's most noteworthy moments. This year's awards show, hosted by Snoop Dogg , is expected to be one for the books .
Three of pop music's most influential names will be celebrated for their remarkable contributions to the genre — and industry — they helped define: Madonna, the Queen of Pop, will return to the VMAs main stage for the first time in over two decades; " Patient Zero " pop star Taylor Swift will make history as the first-ever recipient of the Artist Director Honors; and late, beloved singer George Michael will be honored during a star-studded performance.
Kacey Musgraves is also set to take the stage for a special tribute to Dolly Parton. As if those weren't enough reasons to celebrate, female artists are also leading this year's crop of nominees .
Want the play-by-play? Follow along for Yahoo Entertainment's live coverage below.
Photo illustration: Yahoo News
The VMAs were set to air at 7:30 p.m. ET, but turns out viewers are going to have to wait for the end of the Ravens-Cowboys game to catch the action:
The show is happening, according to our reporters in the room. Madonna has already performed. We just can't see anything until the game is over.
Fashionably late? When you're Taylor Swift, everyone else is simply early. The singer was the last star to hit the VMAs carpet, arriving just minutes before showtime in a sleek black halter bodysuit that gave way to a draped, sparkling silver skirt. She also kept her blunt, shoulder-skimming cut — a look that she debuted just ahead of releasing The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore .
Taylor Swift shuts down the red carpet.
Tonight is very much Swift's night. She'll receive the inaugural Artist Director Honors, which will officially make her the most-awarded artist in VMAs history, while the music video for her new single "Patient Zero" will premiere during the show.
To put it simply: It's Mrs. Kelce's world and we're all just living in it.
Tonight's show hasn't started yet, but the best looks from the VMAs have definitely arrived. The early trends from the red carpet strike a balance between retrospective and current, ranging from an homage to the inaugural show in 1984 to a bold twist on a major trend of the moment. Here's what we're seeing and loving.
In honor of Madonna's return to the VMAs stage tonight, black lace, drastic hemlines, chunky cross jewelry and slogan belts are taking center stage on the carpet.
Bebe Rexha perfectly pays homage to Madonna's iconic look from the inaugural awards show with layers of black lace and a two-bra corset top that Rexha confirmed was inspired by the Queen of Pop.
Bella Kay definitely got the fashion memo and spun it with a choker necklace, combat boots and chunky turquoise jewelry.
Sombr's in-your-face message belt is a not-so-subtle nod to Madge's 1984 VMAs performance. Instead of "Boy Toy," he went with "Sex." Straight to the point.
Teyana Taylor's floor-length gown definitely fits the bill. The long feather trim and oversized fishnet pattern make it one of the boldest looks of the night.
Seeing double? Sophie Silva's outfit is the most exact take on the trend, down to the "Boy Toy" belt.
Yee — and I cannot emphasize this enough — haw . Western wear is all over the red carpet, from cowboy hats to leather touches and corset pants (you read that right).
Orville Peck is giving Zorro-meets-John-Wayne in this masked, fringed leather getup.
Madisin Rian's cowhide look is one of the more intense takes on the trend, and I'm extremely here for it.
Chanel West Coast nails a few trends with this one: high-low hemline, lace, leopard and a bold cowboy hat.
Ciara Miller trades a corset top for a leather bra; her pants, however, make up for it with laces that run from hip to toe.
It wouldn't be the VMAs if there wasn't an ungodly amount of skin showing. These celebs are baring it all for the event.
JoJo's bedazzled black set is neither Too Little nor Too Late.
Charli xcx lets her torso do the talking in an otherwise understated black number. I don't care, I love it.
Tyla's reptilian set quite literally has me lost for words.
Nezza defies logic with a full-length gown that still showcases her entire midsection.
Who just walked by me? Taylor Swift, who will be debuting her "Patient Zero" music video tonight.
Spotted: Charli xcx, who definitely yielded the loudest screams on the carpet. She was moved quickly and did not come down the line for interviews, but I did manage to catch a quick glimpse. My immediate thought: Girl rocks a smoky eye so well.
By taking home the inaugural Artist Director Honors tonight, Taylor Swift is officially the most-awarded artist in VMAs history, surpassing Beyoncé, with whom she was previously tied.
"Across her work, Swift has brought an increasingly expansive approach to storytelling, creating interconnected narratives, cinematic worlds and recurring details that invite audiences deeper into each project," said a press release for Swift's major award. "The inaugural MTV VMA Artist Director Honors recognizes that body of work, while also underscoring the growing role artists play in shaping how their music is brought to life on screen."
On Friday, executive producer Bruce Gillmer told the Associated Press that the award was an "extension" of the Video Vanguard Award, which this year is going to Nirvana. That award is a lifetime achievement honor given to musicians and directors who have made a significant impact on the music video art form.
Gillmer added that "the kernel of the idea" for the new Artist Director Honors "came from external."
He said that the VMAs team put a lot of work into "crafting and thinking about what this could be, the importance of it, [and] launching something as big or bigger than Vanguard."
Swift, who has directed many of her own music videos, has not received the Vanguard award.
It's safe to say Paris Hilton has never met a sequin she didn't like — her iconic 21st birthday dress remains in my brain for all eternity — and tonight she wore all of them. She walked the teal carpet in head-to-toe sparkle: a short, sparkly silver minidress with cutouts, thigh-high boots and matching gloves. And that sleek, sharp-as-a-knife bob is seriously bobbin'! (Hilton is also presenting at tonight's ceremony. )
Paris Hilton is sliving in her sparkles at the VMAS.
Her sister, Nicky Hilton Rothschild, joined her on the carpet in a floor-length, silver sparkly gown, making it a coordinated sister-style moment. That's hot.
The sisters Hilton are bringing double the shine.
Belmont Cameli goes denim on denim.
Chicago native Belmont Cameli may have picked up a few style cues while filming Off Campus north of the border. The actor arrived at the VMAs — where he and costar Ella Bright will serve as presenters — in his take on a Canadian tuxedo, pairing a denim-blue overshirt with darker blue jeans and shiny black shoes.
Love Island star Nic Vansteenberghe has plenty of love to go around for his admirers. When I asked him on the VMAs red carpet who he'd last texted, the reality star retrieved his phone — then revealed he'd been catching up with … a fan! (Sorry to disappoint, Team Nicolandria.)
Tyla went full reptilian for the carpet, wearing a snakeskin bra top with a matching low-slung pencil skirt — and showing plenty of skin of her own in between.
She carried the same theme all the way down to her contrasting snakeskin pumps, because apparently one snake print simply wasn't enough. The singer is also slithering onto the VMAs stage tonight as a presenter.

Welcome to Week 3's Sunday slate! We've got another exciting day of games on deck, including a mid-afternoon international matchup as the Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys travel to Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
The early slate was a busy one, as the Buffalo Bills overcame a five-turnover showing to defeat the Los Angeles Chargers , 24-16. The Jacksonville Jaguars continued to expose Drake Maye and the New England Patriots , who fell to 1-2 as Jacksonville pulled away with a dominant 35-6 win at home. Maye had two interceptions and two fumbles (one lost) as he continues to struggle this season, including one pick nabbed by two-way star Travis Hunter — the first of his career.
Among the biggest surprises of the day was an upset win by the Washington Commanders , as Marcus Mariota started in place of the injured Jayden Daniels (elbow) to pull past the defending Super Bowl champs , 33-31. Mariota played a clean game, tossing for 183 yards, 3 touchdowns and 0 interceptions, while Darnold threw for 379 yards, 4 touchdowns and 2 interceptions, including two that went to reigning Offensive Player of the Year Jaxson Smith-Njigba. That marks six receiving touchdowns for Smith-Njigba through the first three weeks of the season, including three straight games of 120-plus receiving yards.
Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more from Week 3's Sunday game slate.
The Cowboys have all the momentum against the Ravens.
After the Dallas defense forced a turnover on downs at the goal line, Dak Prescott led a 96-yard scoring drive.
It ended with wide receiver KaVontae Turpin running in a 9-yard score on an end-around.
Dallas is now up 28-24 with 9:42 left.
After the Cowboys' run defense got their offense the ball back at the goal line, Dallas was backed up against the end zone.
Dak Prescott launched a ball downfield and found CeeDee Lamb for a 49-yard gain, giving the Cowboys offense plenty of room to operate.
Dallas' rush defense has been shaky to start the season. Baltimore running back Derrick Henry already has two rushing touchdowns.
The Cowboys stood strong, though, and stuffed the Ravens' rushing attack on four consecutive plays, for a combined net loss of a yard over those plays.
With just over 13 minutes left, Baltimore remains up three.
Veteran quarterback punched in a touchdown at the goal line. There was a flag on the play, but it was on the defense, so the score stood.
Arizona now trails San Francisco by just two points.
There are still nine minutes left to go in the Vikings-Buccaneers game. So far, Minnesota's defensive line has sacked Tampa Bay quarterback Baker Mayfield six times.
Brock Purdy tallied his third passing touchdown of the game. He found George Kittle over the middle, who took the ball toward the end zone and then lunged in for the score.
After the play, Eddy Piniero missed his second extra point of the game. San Francisco has a 29-20 lead with 8:42 left in the game.
The Cowboys had been outscored 24-3 since they held an early 10-0 lead.
Dak Prescott found Jake Ferguson for the 19-yard score.
After the TD, Dallas opted to go for two, and CeeDee Lamb came down with the successful conversion.
The Cowboys trail the Ravens 24-21 with 1:48 left in the game.
Raiders backup running back Mike Washington Jr. broke off a 35-yard run. He was initially called short of the goal line, but after review, the rookie was credited with his first career score.
Las Vegas went for two but failed the conversion. The Raiders are down 27-22 with 3:20 left in the third quarter.
Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love has scored his first receiving touchdown of his career. Jacoby Brissett hit him for the 1 -yard score.
The Cardinals are down just three points with 13:06 left in the game.
Saints running back Travis Etienne pulled up after a run and was reaching for his hamstring. He ended up limping to the medical tent for further evaluation and then went to the locker room.
Tyler Shough is clearly hoping for great Christmas presents from his tight ends. The Saints QB now has four touchdowns to tight ends against the Raiders: two to Juwan Johnson and two to Noah Fant.
New Orleans holds a 27-16 lead with 5:46 left in the third quarter.
The Ravens have increased their lead to 11 points as Lamar Jackson found Chris Moore for the four-yard score.
Baltimore is up 24-13 with 3:44 left in the third.
The Buccaneers are struggling to get out of their own way as they try to come back against the Vikings.
Baker Mayfield hit Chris Godwin for a pass, and Godwin dodged defenders all the way to the end zone for the 85-yard score. It was wiped off the board due to a holding call.
It marked back-to-back penalties for the Tampa Bay offense. With 3:50 left in the third quarter, the Bucs have been penalized six times for 61 yards.
The Ravens' special teams unit blocked Brandon Aubrey's 59-yard field goal attempt in the third quarter.
Baltimore's lead remains 4 points.
Tyler Shough and the New Orleans offense went with play action in the red zone.
Tight end Juwan Johnson snuck out the other side of the play, and Shough turned and fired it to him for the duo's second score of the day.
New Orleans now leads Las Vegas 20-16.
The Cardinals trail the 49ers late in the third quarter on Sunday afternoon.
Veteran QB Jacoby Brissett helped his offense find the end zone, cutting the deficit. Brissett connected with Michael Wilson, who dove into the end zone and held on to the ball through contact for the score.
Arizona now trails by 10 with 3:02 left in the third.
Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott tried to shovel a pass to his tight end, Jake Ferguson. The TE barely had the ball as he turned toward the line of scrimmage and was popped. He dropped the ball, and it was ruled a fumble on the field.
After review, the on-field call stood. Rules analyst Gene Steratore disagreed with the call, believing that Ferguson did not have possession of the football long enough for the play to result in a fumble and that it should have been an incomplete pass.
Sometimes it is nice to be reminded of just how athletic defensive linemen are.
Buccaneers defensive tackle A'Shawn Robinson batted a pass from Kyler Murray down at the line of scrimmage. Then, the lineman scooped the ball off the ground after it bounced off several players.
It is still unclear exactly when Justin Jefferson picked up his injury, but he hadn't been in the game since early in the first quarter.
The star wide receiver has been ruled out for the remainder of the game. He finishes the day with 32 yards on two receptions.
Read more from Yahoo Sports .
The injuries for the 49ers continue to mount. After Mike Evans was ruled out for the remainder of the game, offensive tackle Trent Williams was carted to the locker room with a towel on his head.
Williams is reportedly dealing with a stinger .

Takeaways from the Giants’ 12-7 win over the Titans at MetLife Stadium on Sunday.
1. Well, it was not exactly a nor’easter but it was a windy and wet day for football. There were plenty of empty seats and that was not because Jaxson Dart is out for the season or because the Titans are not a marquee draw. Sometimes, fans do not want to sit out there for three hours in uncomfortable conditions. On the field, the wind did not seem to wreak too much havoc with the passing game — the struggles seemed more about the quarterbacks, Jameis Winston and Cam Ward, than the weather. After the raucous environment two weeks ago for the season-opening victory over the Cowboys, this was a far more subdued afternoon.
Get texts from Paul Schwartz with all the latest Giants news and insights, exclusive to Sports+ subscribers.
2 .  Malik Nabers looked quite excited, gesturing with full enthusiasm that he picked up the first down on a 12-yard reception on the first play of the Giants’ final possession in the fourth quarter. Nabers made the catch against former teammate Cor’Dale Flott, which must have felt good. As it turned out, that was Nabers’ longest reception of the game. He caught five passes for only 26 yards and was actually the most productive wide receiver (Darnell Mooney had 20 receiving yards and rookie Malachi Fields had 19). It was that sort of sluggish day for the passing attack. Sure, the weather was not conducive for long-range throws but there were enough throws by Jameis Winston that could have been completed that he failed to deliver. Games like this can frustrate wide receivers. It is something to monitor.
3. Coaching matters. Titans head coach Robert Saleh sent Joey Slye out to try a 59-yard field goal with 41 seconds remaining in the first half. Yes, Slye was kicking with the wind and yes, he was hitting them from long distance in the pregame warmup. Still, it was not exactly a high-percentage play. The Titans were down 6-0 so they were right in this low-scoring affair. Punting the ball away would be fine. Slye had the distance but missed wide left, giving the Giants the ball on their 49-yard line. From there, all that was needed was two first downs to set Dominic Zvada up for a 39-yard field goal as time expired. Instead of being down one score, the Titans trailed 9-0. Big difference.

articles.title_zh: 5 arrested in U.K. near base used by U.S. on suspicion of planning terror act
articles.content_orig:
LONDON — British police arrested several men on suspicion of terrorism and explosives offenses Sunday and evacuated homes near an air base that the U.S. Air Force had been using to facilitate strikes on Iran.
A major incident was declared, with a massive emergency presence seen around RAF Fairford, which is about 90 minutes outside London, close to the village of Whelford in western England.
The Gloucestershire police force said it responded in the early hours of Sunday to reports of three suspicious vehicles moving toward the base, and arrested five men “on suspicion of committing offenses under the Explosives Act.” They were later further charged on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act.
Police did not provide further details on the men, who remain in custody, or what they were suspected to have done. “Work to establish the full nature of this incident is ongoing,” Assistant Chief Constable Richard Ocone said.
Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans of Counter Terrorism Policing said the force is “working closely with our partners to understand the circumstances of the incident,” with the investigation still in its “early stages.”
Ocone said 85 homes across the local area were evacuated and a 440-yard cordon put in place while an Army ordnance disposal team examines the vehicles.
Helicopter footage from Sky News showed multiple white vans close to the base seemingly being searched by a bomb disposal robot.
Julian Tudsbery, who has lived in Whelford for 30 years, told Britain’s Press Association another resident had reported three suspicious vans in the village. Along with other residents, Tudsbery has since been evacuated to a nearby recreation center.
The Reuters news agency had reported that security measures at the air ‌base have been significantly increased in recent ‌days.
Cotswold District Council member Tristan Wilkinson told NBC News that a threat to the base from Iran about six weeks ago has heightened the alert level in the community and led to a ramped-up police presence and an increase in security patrols.
Wilkinson noted there is “a lot more vigilance from the local community” and that police in this instance “have done exactly what you’d hope they would do in increasing reassurance for the community.”
“This is a worry and escalation, and we wait to see what the nature of that actual incident is going to be,” the official added.
A U.S. European Command spokesperson said: “For operational security reasons we will not discuss specific force protection measures.”
“U.S. European Command remains vigilant and will take appropriate actions to ensure the safety and security of our U.S. service members, civilians, contractors, and their families across the European theater,” the spokesperson added. “We constantly assess a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people and their families.”
Asked about the incident Sunday after walking off Air Force One, President Donald Trump told reporters the arrest was an “amazing job.”
“They were looking to do big damage to our fort, and working with the British worked out great,” he said.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said in a post on X: “I know today’s incident near RAF Fairford will be deeply concerning for local residents and for many people following developments across the country.”
“The safety and security of the public is our first priority, and I want people to know that we will always take every step necessary to protect our communities and keep our country safe,” he added.
“The investigation remains ongoing, and I would urge people not to speculate while the authorities establish the full facts,” Burnham said.
In March, Keir Starmer , Burnham’s predecessor, gave permission for the U.S. to use its bases for “specific and limited defensive” operations against Iran.
In July, Iran’s ⁠Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps warned Britain that “any base used to invade Iranian territory is our legitimate target,” Iran’s semiofficial Tasnim news agency reported, citing bomber aircraft flights from Fairford.
At the time, a British government spokesperson said that the country was “ready to keep the United Kingdom safe from any kind of attacks, whether it’s on our soil or from abroad.”
Freddie Clayton is a freelance journalist based in London.
Courtney Kube is a correspondent covering national security and the military for the NBC News Investigative Unit.
Raf Sanchez is a foreign correspondent for NBC News.

Serbia's president has resigned after more than a year of student-led protests and growing public discontent over allegations of government corruption.
Aleksandar VuÄiÄ said his administration had preserved peace and stability during his nine-year tenure as he addressed supporters outside the presidential building in the capital, Belgrade.
He had already announced his intention to resign in June and is currently standing to be his party's candidate for prime minister in the upcoming parliamentary elections. VuÄiÄ cannot run for a third presidential term under Serbia's constitution.
The pro-Russian populist's administration has been dogged by anger over alleged corner-cutting.
It was the collapse of the Novi Sad railway station's roof , killing 16 people, that first galvanised anger towards the government in 2024.
Protests involving a wide range of citizens - from students and teachers to workers and farmers - followed.
Demonstrators believed that the disaster reflected more than a decade of governing by the Progressive Party of Vucic, who closely associated himself with the station's renovation, which was supposed to be a symbol of Serbia's progress.
A series of resignations of those under the embattled president failed to placate the protesters, who continued to demonstrate throughout this summer, turning to unrest following accusations of police brutality .
VuÄiÄ's presidency was due to expire next year. Under Serbia's constitution, presidential elections must be held no more than three months after his resignation.
This means Serbians will go to the polls twice before the end of the year.
VuÄiÄ said the presidential election will take place more than a month after the snap parliamentary election in late October, itself called in response to the protests, which had added calls for a vote to their list of demands.
He had earlier announced that he planned to run in that election as Progressive Party's leader, leaving the possibility he could retain a position at the top of Serbian politics.
Parliamentary speaker Ana BrnabiÄ, also a Progressive Party member, will assume the role of interim president until a new one is elected.
VuÄiÄ used his constitutional powers to pardon 49 people, including 23 students and party loyalists suspected of offences related to what he called the "terrible events we have gone through over the past year and a half", according to Serbian public broadcaster RTS.
The upcoming parliamentary elections will pit VuÄiÄ's Progressive Party against a student-led, anti-corruption movement called Students Win and a coalition of pro-Western opposition parties known as European Serbia.
Vucic has been a fixture of Serbian politics for more than a decade , becoming prime minister in 2014, before being elected to his first term as president in 2017.
He has publicly said he wants Serbia to join the EU while courting close ties with Russia and opening Serbia up to Chinese investment.

Madonna is set to take the stage as a performer at the MTV Video Music Awards for the first time in over 20 years today as she looks to add to her 20 career wins at the VMAs.
The awards show also brings a milestone for Taylor Swift , who will be given the VMAs' first-ever Artist Director Honors, which organizers said recognizes artists "whose work behind the camera has expanded the possibilities of music video and advanced the art of visual storytelling."
The new accolade guarantees that Swift, who's also nominated in 11 categories, will become the show's most-awarded artist, breaking the tie between her and Beyoncé, who each collected 30 Moon Persons as of 2024 . (Neither added to their total in 2025 .)
Swift will also be debuting her new "Patient Zero" music video at the VMAs.
Nirvana, meanwhile, will be this year's Video Vanguard Award recipient.
The show starts at 7:30 p.m. ET, 4:30 p.m. PT, on Sunday, Sept. 27.
This year's show is being hosted by Snoop Dogg. The rapper known for hits like "Beautiful," "Drop It Like It's Hot" and "Gin and Juice" is no stranger to the VMAs stage, having first performed at the show in 1994 and winning three times during his career.
The VMAs will be airing on CBS television stations ( find your local station here ) and on MTV . The show will also be streaming on Paramount+ .
See the stars arrive and check out the best looks from the red carpet in special coverage streaming live on CBS News Los Angeles starting at 6 p.m. ET, 3 p.m. PT, ahead of the VMAs.

This year, a performance by the 68-year-old Queen of Pop will open the VMAs. She's up for 13 awards, the most of any nominee of the night. If she sweeps all 13 categories, her career total will go up to 33.

Coastal communities across the Northeast faced more flooding and power outages on Sunday as a powerful nor’easter continued to lash the region , with forecasters warning that upcoming high tides could further submerge vulnerable shorelines.
The slow-moving storm —which resulted in a fatality on Saturday when a falling tree struck a New York City housing authority worker—was expected to persist through Sunday with heavy rain, high winds, and dangerous surf from New Jersey to New England.
Positioned south of Long Island and east of northern New Jersey on Sunday morning, the storm was forecast to loop around the region for roughly another 24 hours, said Bob Oravec, a lead forecaster with the National Weather Service in College Park, Maryland.
Meteorologists expected the heaviest remaining rainfall on Sunday to span northern New Jersey through New York City and Long Island into southern New England. While the system was gradually losing strength, Oravec noted that the threat of tidal flooding would persist during morning and evening high-tide cycles.
"The most impactful parts of the storm are likely going to be the high winds and the tidal flooding," Oravec said.
The weather evoked memories of 2012's Superstorm Sandy, which caused over $60 billion in damage across the eastern US. Although the current impact remains far lower, it could mark the first of several East Coast storms this fall influenced by an El Niño climate pattern.
More than 130,000 customers lost electricity across the Northeast and mid-Atlantic by Sunday morning, according to PowerOutage.us.
The most severe outages affected the New Jersey coastline, Long Island, and coastal Connecticut. Fallen trees across Long Island damaged homes and vehicles, blocked roads, and severed power lines.
The Federal Emergency Management Agency stated that regional response centers were operating at an "enhanced posture," with emergency personnel staged in New England in case of widespread blackouts.
On Saturday, flooded streets in New York and New Jersey saw residents kayaking, while others attempted to surf elevated waves at local beaches. Emergency crews in Sea Bright, New Jersey, rescued a woman and her dog trapped in a flooded vehicle, ABC7 reported.
In Surf City, New Jersey, floodwaters entered a marina where staff had relocated equipment, and owner Kenny Formica said clients reported missing boats and Jet Skis blown from lifts. In Norfolk, Virginia, high waters left driving cars pushing wakes through streets.
Travel across the region was also upended. Hundreds of flights were grounded at Boston Logan International Airport, and flooding cut highway access to Hatteras Island, North Carolina, stranding tourists and forcing a couple to relocate their wedding when roughly 45 guests could not reach the island.

articles.title_orig: OpenAI Agents Hit U.S. Government Websites
articles.title_zh: OpenAI Agents Hit U.S. Government Websites
articles.content_orig:
OpenAI said in a technical report released on Friday that an AI model it was training and evaluating broke out of its secure testing environment as recently as last weekend and took unauthorized actions on the internet. As a result, the company said that it is pausing the training of its most advanced AI models for the second time in less than three months while it tries to figure out how to stop these “rogue AI” incidents from recurring.
“All inference for our most capable models remains stopped until we have hardened our systems further,” Micah Carroll, the RSI Preparedness Lead at OpenAI, said in a post on X about the latest incident. The company said the latest incident occurred on Sept. 20. It involved an AI agent undergoing tests on an information-search task. Even though it was not supposed to have access to the internet, the agent found a way to send queries to a public chatbot. The new revelation is significant because it is the first time the company has said that one of its AI models was able to gain unauthorized internet access since announcing a range of steps on Aug. 18 to improve the security and monitoring of its “sandboxes”—the digital environments, usually walled off from network and internet access, in which it tests unreleased models in order to discover their capabilities. Those improvements followed the July incident in which thousands of OpenAI’s AI agents found a way to hack out of their sandbox, with hundreds of them participating in a cyberattack against the AI company Hugging Face.
Since disclosing its role in the Hugging Face attack, OpenAI has acknowledged dozens more incidents in which AI agents it was testing took unauthorized actions across the internet, including multiple cyber attacks, some of which impacted government websites in the U.S. and Australia. It also has revealed that in some of these incidents its AI agents leaked private images from ChatGPT users to the internet. But until now, OpenAI has not reported any activity taking place after July 20, when it discovered the agent swarm that was attacking Hugging Face and moved to shut it down. The company said it had paused AI training in late July for two weeks while it worked to improve its security and safety controls and monitoring. The fact that its AI agents have once again managed to break out of a sandbox suggests that the steps OpenAI has taken to improve security after the Hugging Face attack are insufficient. “The incident exposed a gap in our controls over network restrictions,” OpenAI said in its technical report on the Sept. 20 sandbox escape. It said it was once again pausing training until it has “both validated that the gap is resolved and performed additional red-teaming of the system.”
Asked about the Sept. 20 incident, an OpenAI spokesperson referred Fortune to a section of the technical incident report in which OpenAI described some of the actions it has taken to improve security and control since the Hugging Face attack. “Following the Hugging Face incident, we have continuously hardened and red-teamed our research environment,” that section reads. “Our focus has been broad direct and transitive paths. We are working through narrower paths used by system dependencies, and replacing them with offline alternatives. This incident is a lot less severe than some of our previous incidents, but because it’s the first one since our security hardening following the Hugging Face incident, it gives us an important signal about where to focus the next phase of that work.”
In this case, OpenAI said the AI agent had discovered that it had access to a service called a DNS resolver, which translates between a website URL and an IP address, and that through this DNS system it could send queries to a public chatbot.
It is not clear if the Sept. 20 episode reported by OpenAI represents the full extent of the latest security lapses involving the company’s unreleased AI models. Earlier this week, independent AI research firm Transluce AI said it had found evidence that an OpenAI AI agent may have attempted to hack a cryptocurrency exchange on Sept. 19 and Sept. 20. OpenAI has not replied to requests to comment on this aspect of the Transluce report. OpenAI said that when it restarts training, it will begin from scratch to hopefully ensure the new model’s tendency to engage in “misaligned” behavior—when a model violates human instructions or common sense human values about how it should and should not accomplish a task—is expunged. It also said that it would institute “more comprehensive misalignment interventions” but did not specify what these would be.
The company said that since discovering this latest security lapse it has “added blocking controls at two independent layers, either of which would have prevented [the agent’s] internet access.” OpenAI also disclosed that systems it had put in place after the Hugging Face attack to catch AI agents attempting to break out of their test sandboxes only partly worked. On top of that, an additional system that was automatically supposed to stop training runs once misaligned behavior was detected had failed. The company said its monitoring systems “flagged the [agent’s] behavior within 15 minutes and a person began reviewing it three minutes after that.” But a subsequent review found there had been other attempts by the AI model to use the same method to reach the internet that had not been flagged by the monitoring system. A different system that was supposed to automatically shut down the training run when suspicious activity is detected did not work, “leading to confusion around whether it should have been stopped,” OpenAI said in the technical report on the incident. “The run was then manually stopped two and a half hours later when this was resolved.” Zuxin Liu, an AI researcher who works on “post-training” at OpenAI, said in a post on X that he was one of the employees called in to respond to the Sept. 20 sandbox escape. “It was pretty surreal to watch the model unexpectedly find a way to access the internet from what was supposed to be a super secured environment for human,” he wrote.
Update, Sept 26: This story has been updated to include a response from OpenAI to Fortune’s question about this latest incident.

articles.title_orig: Giant pandas Ping Ping and Fu Shuang arrive in Atlanta from China - ABC News
articles.title_zh: Giant pandas Ping Ping and Fu Shuang arrive in Atlanta from China - ABC News
articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
Two giant pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, have arrived in the US state of Georgia on a 10-year loan as a soft-power gesture from China.
A new agreement between Zoo Atlanta and the China Wildlife Conservation Association makes Atlanta one of three zoos in the US to house giant pandas .
The diplomatic gifts departed early on Sunday from Chengdu Shuangliu International Airport in southwestern China, according to Chinese state media. They arrived after the high-level three-day Washington summit with China last week, where closed-door talks between United States President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping yielded no major policy breakthroughs on prickly issues such as AI, trade, Taiwan and the war with Iran.
Although the pandas’ transfer had been finalised back in April, Xi officially announced the arrival timeline on Thursday at the White House, noting that the black and white mammals could reach Zoo Atlanta from the Chengdu Research Base, China’s premier hub for giant panda conservation, breeding and research, within the next few days. The dispatch of the vulnerable species aimed to signal a renewed bilateral friendship between the leaders of the world’s two biggest economies.
Ahead of their arrival, Zoo Atlanta had upgraded its panda habitats and secured a stable, long-term supply of locally grown Atlanta bamboo, which shares a near-identical climate with Chengdu.
The bears completed a 16-hour charter flight across the International Date Line, landing in Atlanta, Georgia, shortly before 7:00am (11:00am GMT).
Midway through its journey through Alaska, the FedEx Boeing 777 had spiked to the top of Flightradar24’s global tracking charts.
Steamed corn buns, bamboo shoots and carrots were prepared to keep the pandas nourished during their flight, Chinese state-run media reported. The US also mobilised a specialised care team to accompany the duo on their flight, they said.
A spokesperson for the zoo told Al Jazeera that their team had “done everything possible to accommodate them”, but a definitive timeline for their arrival – much less their public debut – remains “unconfirmed”.
“This is a thrilling day for Zoo Atlanta and a historic moment for the City of Atlanta, the state of Georgia and beyond,” Zoo Atlanta President and CEO Raymond B. King said in a statement. “We are elated to welcome Ping Ping and Fu Shuang and could not be more excited about sharing that joy with our Members, guests, city and community in the coming weeks.”
Zoo visitors will have to wait a while to see Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, officials said. The bears will be quarantined for about a month in a biosecure area of the wildlife park’s new giant panda complex. The zoo last had pandas in 2024.
Ping Ping, a male, and Fu Shuang, a female, were born in 2020.
Globally revered, the iconic furry animals have been sent across the globe for decades, serving as diplomatic emissaries loaned by China under its infamous “panda diplomacy” initiative through soft-power projection. Beijing leverages the animals’ immense public appeal to cultivate international goodwill, seal lucrative trade deals and burnish its geopolitical image abroad. Similarly, when foreign relationships fray or tensions arise, Beijing lets the loan agreements expire.
Xi has said this latest loan programme was an example of “friendship between the Chinese and Americans”.
Last week’s summit was Xi’s first visit to Washington in more than a decade and the second meeting this year with Trump.
Tangible outcomes of the meetings remain modest , restricted to a two-month extension of the trade truce, Beijing’s revival of giant panda loans and Xi’s support for Trump’s rebranding of artificial intelligence as “super intelligence”.

articles.content_orig:
Eleven people in their late teens were shot overnight Sunday at a park in Georgia, according to law enforcement.
The Bibb County Sheriff's Office said the shooting occurred around midnight "at a large gathering" in Carolyn Crayton Park in the city of Macon, about 85 miles southeast of Atlanta. The wounded victims were identified as four 18-year-old men, two 18-year-old women and five 17-year-old boys, according to the sheriff's office.
Two of the victims, an 18-year-old man and a 17-year-old boy, were in critical condition, authorities said. The others were in stable condition.
The gathering appeared to be a birthday party that was originally supposed to take place at an Airbnb in Jones County, but the host made the group leave the premises, according to Bibb County Sheriff David Davis. The group included several students from nearby Central High School and Northeast High School, Davis said.
After the birthday party attendees gathered at the park, another group arrived and an argument between the two groups escalated into gunfire, Davis told reporters at a news conference.
All the victims were part of the party, Davis added, saying that he "can't remember the last time we've had this many people shot at one time."

Amid a fast-growing international debate over regulating artificial intelligence, President Trump and Chinese President Xi met at the White House for several hours on Thursday ahead of a state dinner where several of the biggest players in A.I. were set to attend.
“We had a great meeting,” Trump said later that afternoon at the Southern Portico, where he gave Xi a tour of the South Lawn Helipad .
“He’s an expert on stones, and he loves good granite,” Trump said of Xi.
The day began with remarks from both Trump and Xi at the grand foyer of the White House. Afterward, Trump and Xi participated in a military review at the Rose Garden and took part in hours of meetings before Trump led a tour of parts of the White House.
While both leaders mentioned AI in their opening remarks, Xi stressed that the development of AI always needs to be “under human control.”
Trump was set to host a state dinner for Xi Thursday evening, joined by a slate of tech leaders. Amazon Executive Chairman Jeff Bezos, Google CEO Sundar Pichai, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Tesla CEO Elon Musk were set to attend the dinner, a White House official confirmed.
According to Chinese state media, President Xi raised the issue of Iran during the bilateral meeting, saying that he hoped the US and Iran would resume negotiations and that China would support the two countries recommitting to the 14-point memorandum of understanding reached months ago.
On Taiwan, Xi said he hopes the U.S. would maintain its position of opposing Taiwan independence. The U.S. has not officially endorsed Taiwan's independence, but has previously sold weaponry to the island and is widely viewed as a key player if China were to ever invade the self-ruling island.
Earlier on Thursday, Xi urged more cooperation between the two countries. During his remarks, he called for more direct flights between the U.S. and China and invited 100,000 American students for cultural exchange in the next five years. And continuing a longtime diplomatic tradition stretching back to the Nixon era, he announced two pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, will be delivered to Zoo Atlanta in the coming days.
“China and the United States must hold the line of no conflict and no confrontation between us, and we can certainly find the right path for two great countries to get along on this planet we both call home,” Xi said.
This is the first time a Chinese leader has made a second formal state visit to America. The last time Xi conducted a formal state visit in Washington, D.C. was at the invitation of President Obama in September 2015, three years after he succeeded as the General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party.
Trump and Xi first met in 2017, during Trump’s first term, at the President’s home base of Mar-a-Lago, Florida. The pair last met in May during a two-day state visit by Trump to Beijing, where the U.S. and China delegations discussed a range of topics including tariffs, rare mineral trade, as well as the Strait of Hormuz. The two leaders used the visit to announce the launch of a so-called Board of Trade intended to lower tariffs on products that aren’t considered a national security risk. In June, the Office of the United States Trade Representative asked the public to weigh in on which types of products would benefit from this new mechanism. The Administration has offered few updates on the board since then.

Waltz says Trump rejected Iran’s proposal to end war because they ‘were asking for everything up front’
The Trump administration ’s ambassador to the United Nations said the US rejected Iran ’s proposal to end the ongoing war there because Iranian negotiators “were asking for everything up front”.
Echoing comments by Donald Trump on Saturday, the president’s UN ambassador Mike Waltz told CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday that Iran had asked for relief “from billions and billions of sanctions that are going into place” as part of an economic blockade on Iran. The blockade is aimed at putting pressure on Iran to stop its attacks ‌on vessels in the strait of Hormuz.
“They were asking for everything up front with a promise that they would then talk,” Waltz said on State of the Union. “The president is just not confident that the Iranians are coming in good faith and that we will truly negotiate the end of their nuclear program.”
Trump said on Saturday that he had rejected Iran’s peace plan, proposed at ⁠the recent UN general assembly in New York, arguing that desperation was driving the Iranians’ push for an agreement on the key waterway. “They want to make a deal ⁠to open the Hormuz strait immediately because they’re losing so badly,” Trump said.
Trump said the US was “winning tremendously” and had “total control of the Hormuz strait”.
In comments to Axios on Sunday, Trump said he expected more talks with Iran during the upcoming week. “They want to make a deal, but it is not the deal that I want to make,” the outlet quoted the president as saying. “It is what we would have maybe agreed to a year ago. They overplayed their hand.”
Earlier, Waltz pointed to the failed US-Iran memorandum of understanding (MOU) signed in Pakistan in June that laid out a 14-point framework agreement for a negotiated peace.
Iran, he said, “immediately violated it by attacking international shipping, in violation of international law, and 146 nations have joined us in condemning Iran for those attacks”.
Iran on Sunday insisted that only diplomacy can solve its conflict with the US and Israel.
“Our conditions are clear, ​and any move toward reopening the strait of Hormuz is contingent on these conditions being met,” the Iranian foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, posted on social media. “Only a negotiated solution can get them out of this deadlock.”
Araghchi also appeared on NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday, saying his country is prepared to resume fighting with the US but has not yet abandoned diplomacy after Trump rejected Iran’s peace proposal.
“We are fully prepared for the war to be resumed,” Araghchi said. “We stand firm in the face of any new aggression, even if it comes to a doomsday war.
“At the same time, we stand ready for diplomacy. It is up to President Trump to choose.”
The Iranian president, Masoud Pezeshkian, in an interview with the CBS show Face the Nation, said his country was ready for ​talks on its nuclear program and other issues – but would not ​accept “bullying or coercion”.
“Iran is not seeking war, but will ​defend itself against pressure, threats and attacks,” Pezeshkian said, adding that it had already agreed that “we’re not supposed to develop nuclear weapons”.

On CNN, Waltz also addressed recent reports that China had assisted Iran in missile targeting of shipping in the strait of Hormuz and on US military bases in the region.
Waltz did not confirm the leaked intelligence assessments but said Trump had raised the issue with China premier Xi Jinping during the latter’s recent state visit to the US capital Washington DC. Trump had also done so “multiple times” previously, including during his visit to China in May, according to Waltz.
“I think we have seen movement in a positive direction,” Waltz said. “President Trump has made it clear it’s unacceptable.”
Waltz pointed to readouts of the high-level meeting that said the US and China had “agreed that Iran can never have a nuclear weapon”.
“They cannot and should not be tolling, much less attacking, international shipping in an international waterway,” Waltz said. “So I think that was incredibly important to hear from President Xi coming out of the summit.”
Waltz also rejected reporting in the Wall Street Journal that the US would resume bombing Iran after the federal midterm elections in November. He pointed to Trump’s comments that Iran was miscalculating.
“The president is looking to make not just this generation – but the next generation – safer by not allowing what is essentially a terrorist organization in [Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps] that is controlling the levers of government and wants to march towards a nuclear weapon,” Waltz said. “We’re not going to let the IRGC have a nuclear weapon, much less hold the world hostage with one.”

articles.title_zh: Anthropic CEO Amodei set to meet with Trump after missing state dinner
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei will join President Donald Trump for a private dinner at the White House on Sunday, CNBC confirmed, in what will be the first one-on-one meeting between the two leaders.
Amodei was noticeably absent from Trump's glitzy state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday, as other tech bigwigs — OpenAI CEO Sam Altman , SpaceX CEO Elon Musk , Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg — were photographed rubbing elbows with government officials. Amodei had a scheduling conflict, so Trump invited him to a private dinner, according to a source familiar with the details who was not authorized to speak publicly.
The meeting, first reported by Axios , comes at a high-stakes moment for Anthropic, which is gearing up for what's widely expected to be a blockbuster IPO . The company's precarious relationship with the Trump administration has been under strain for much of the last year, so Amodei's sit-down with the president could serve as a valuable opportunity to ease tensions.
"President Trump has been clear: America will lead the world in Super Intelligence, while protecting American consumers," a White House official said in a statement, in response to CNBC's inquiry about Sunday's dinner. "We will drive innovation, strengthen American competitiveness, and ensure this transformative technology works for the American people."
Amodei drew Trump's ire earlier this month by publicly urging the AI industry to slow down the pace of advanced model development and better address potential risks . He published a three-step proposal and called for additional government oversight, which angered the president even as it gained the support of other industry leaders like Altman and Musk.
"The only control or 'guardrails' that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!," Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social . "The Trump Administration has stopped AI 'people' from doing bad, or potentially bad, 'things,' like Dario (Anthropic!), who is now pretending to be a 'perfect little angel' - and we will continue to do so!"
Amodei was already in a difficult spot with the president, because he supported Kamala Harris in the 2024 presidential election and was a vocal critic of Trump.
But before Amodei's call for a slowdown rocked the tech sector, Anthropic's relationship with the Trump administration appeared to be on the mend.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who temporarily imposed export controls on two of the company's most advanced models in June, told Axios earlier this month that Anthropic is "back on the right side." He also hosted a fireside chat with Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown at the G20 Innovation Ministerial in North Carolina.
Brown, who serves as Anthropic's chief compute officer, has taken on a much more active role in interfacing with the Trump administration in recent months. He reportedly led the company's negotiations with the Commerce Department over its export control directive, replacing Amodei in that role.
"We trust Anthropic," Lutnick said on the sidelines of the event.
That same day, White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) Director Michael Kratsios told CNBC that the administration was "in a good cadence" with Anthropic. He said the company was "open" and actively sharing models with the government as part of Trump's voluntary AI executive order.
Anthropic has had less success winning over officials at the Department of Defense, however.
Negotiations between the company and the Pentagon spiraled in February after the two sides failed to agree on how the military could use its models. The DOD wanted Anthropic to grant the military unfettered access to its models across all lawful purposes, while Anthropic wanted assurance that its technology would not be used for fully autonomous weapons or domestic mass surveillance.
After talks collapsed, the DOD labeled Anthropic a supply chain risk , an unprecedented move that meant the company purportedly threatened U.S. national security. The designation prevents the U.S. military from using Anthropic's models and blocks defense contractors from using them in their work with the agency.
Anthropic sued the Trump administration in an effort to reverse it's blacklisting, but the company suffered a blow on Friday after a federal appeals court panel in Washington, D.C., upheld the Pentagon's action . The company could still petition for a rehearing, and could also ask the Supreme Court to take the case.
Emil Michael, the DOD's technology chief, celebrated the ruling in a post on X .
"The hammer of justice has smashed @AnthropicAI arguments," Michael wrote on Friday. "They are a Supply Chain Risk to the defense industrial base serving the @DeptofWar. Warfighters will sleep better knowing that no private company will insert their opinions in the chain of command. @SecWar was right!"
Defense Secretary Hegseth accused Anthropic of "duplicity" and argued that the company attempted "to strong-arm the United States military into submission" when negotiations collapsed in February. He reaffirmed that position in a post on X on Friday.
"Confirmed: @AnthropicAI = Supply Chain Risk," Hegseth wrote. The @DeptofWar does what is right for the Country and our Warriors."

articles.title_zh: Amodei critics target Trump with hit piece before White House dinner
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei will join President Donald Trump for a private dinner at the White House on Sunday, CNBC confirmed, in what will be the first one-on-one meeting between the two leaders.
Amodei was noticeably absent from Trump's glitzy state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday, as other tech bigwigs — OpenAI CEO Sam Altman , SpaceX CEO Elon Musk , Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg — were photographed rubbing elbows with government officials. Amodei had a scheduling conflict, so Trump invited him to a private dinner, according to a source familiar with the details who was not authorized to speak publicly.
The meeting, first reported by Axios , comes at a high-stakes moment for Anthropic, which is gearing up for what's widely expected to be a blockbuster IPO . The company's precarious relationship with the Trump administration has been under strain for much of the last year, so Amodei's sit-down with the president could serve as a valuable opportunity to ease tensions.
"President Trump has been clear: America will lead the world in Super Intelligence, while protecting American consumers," a White House official said in a statement, in response to CNBC's inquiry about Sunday's dinner. "We will drive innovation, strengthen American competitiveness, and ensure this transformative technology works for the American people."
Amodei drew Trump's ire earlier this month by publicly urging the AI industry to slow down the pace of advanced model development and better address potential risks . He published a three-step proposal and called for additional government oversight, which angered the president even as it gained the support of other industry leaders like Altman and Musk.
"The only control or 'guardrails' that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!," Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social . "The Trump Administration has stopped AI 'people' from doing bad, or potentially bad, 'things,' like Dario (Anthropic!), who is now pretending to be a 'perfect little angel' - and we will continue to do so!"
Amodei was already in a difficult spot with the president, because he supported Kamala Harris in the 2024 presidential election and was a vocal critic of Trump.
But before Amodei's call for a slowdown rocked the tech sector, Anthropic's relationship with the Trump administration appeared to be on the mend.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who temporarily imposed export controls on two of the company's most advanced models in June, told Axios earlier this month that Anthropic is "back on the right side." He also hosted a fireside chat with Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown at the G20 Innovation Ministerial in North Carolina.
Brown, who serves as Anthropic's chief compute officer, has taken on a much more active role in interfacing with the Trump administration in recent months. He reportedly led the company's negotiations with the Commerce Department over its export control directive, replacing Amodei in that role.
"We trust Anthropic," Lutnick said on the sidelines of the event.
That same day, White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) Director Michael Kratsios told CNBC that the administration was "in a good cadence" with Anthropic. He said the company was "open" and actively sharing models with the government as part of Trump's voluntary AI executive order.
Anthropic has had less success winning over officials at the Department of Defense, however.
Negotiations between the company and the Pentagon spiraled in February after the two sides failed to agree on how the military could use its models. The DOD wanted Anthropic to grant the military unfettered access to its models across all lawful purposes, while Anthropic wanted assurance that its technology would not be used for fully autonomous weapons or domestic mass surveillance.
After talks collapsed, the DOD labeled Anthropic a supply chain risk , an unprecedented move that meant the company purportedly threatened U.S. national security. The designation prevents the U.S. military from using Anthropic's models and blocks defense contractors from using them in their work with the agency.
Anthropic sued the Trump administration in an effort to reverse it's blacklisting, but the company suffered a blow on Friday after a federal appeals court panel in Washington, D.C., upheld the Pentagon's action . The company could still petition for a rehearing, and could also ask the Supreme Court to take the case.
Emil Michael, the DOD's technology chief, celebrated the ruling in a post on X .
"The hammer of justice has smashed @AnthropicAI arguments," Michael wrote on Friday. "They are a Supply Chain Risk to the defense industrial base serving the @DeptofWar. Warfighters will sleep better knowing that no private company will insert their opinions in the chain of command. @SecWar was right!"
Defense Secretary Hegseth accused Anthropic of "duplicity" and argued that the company attempted "to strong-arm the United States military into submission" when negotiations collapsed in February. He reaffirmed that position in a post on X on Friday.
"Confirmed: @AnthropicAI = Supply Chain Risk," Hegseth wrote. The @DeptofWar does what is right for the Country and our Warriors."

articles.content_orig:
Thom Tillis says Trump’s decision to back Paxton over John Cornyn has put the Senate seat at risk for Republicans
US senator Thom Tillis on Sunday criticized Donald Trump , his fellow Republican, for the president’s support of Ken Paxton over incumbent John Cornyn in the Texas Senate Republican primary.
“He made a colossal mistake,” Tillis, a frequent Trump critic from North Carolina, said during an interview on CNN’s State of the Union in reference to the president’s support of Paxton who defeated Cornyn in the May primary.
“John Cornyn’s a great member of the US Senate. Paxton has his challenges,” the retiring Tillis added. “We would not be spending tens or hundreds of millions of dollars in Texas if Cornyn had won.”
Tillis pointed to the president’s involvement in the contest and described Trump’s decision to back Paxton instead of Cornyn as an “unforced error” that has put the Senate seat at risk for the GOP.
Trump endorsed Paxton just days before the Texas attorney general defeated Cornyn, a four-term senator, and advanced to face Democratic candidate James Talarico, a in the general election on 3 November.
The race had wide implications for Trump’s strength heading into November’s midterm federal elections. Paxton will now face Talarico, a Democratic pastor and state legislator whose message of peace and populism has attracted much attention. If he wins, Talarico would become the first Democrat in more than 30 years to win statewide office in Texas.
When he chose to support Paxton over Cornyn, Trump highlighted the Texas attorney general’s record as a steadfast supporter of the president’s Make America Great Again (Maga) movement.
Cornyn had previously said during the 2024 presidential campaign that Republicans should move on from Trump.
In a social media post shortly before the election day, Trump said Cornyn had been “VERY disloyal” to him and implored voters in Texas to “REMEMBER!”
Paxton, meanwhile, is struggling to overcome a series of political scandals. He was impeached in 2023 after being accused of corruption and later acquitted in a trial in the Texas senate. He was also indicted on charges of felony securities fraud, but the case was dismissed after a 2024 pretrial diversion agreement.
In July 2025, his wife of 38 years, Angela Paxton, filed for divorce “ on biblical grounds ”, citing adultery.
Tillis is one of a handful of Republicans to repeatedly break with Trump and publicly criticize the president’s decisions. In April, he spoke out in defense of the Nato military alliance after Trump said he was “absolutely” considering withdrawing the US from it.
“Any president that contemplates attempting to withdraw from Nato is not only fulfilling [Russian leader] Vladimir Putin and [Chinese premier] Xi Jinping’s greatest dreams but would be undermining America’s own national security interests,” Tillis said at the time.
He also called for then secretary of homeland security Kristi Noem’s resignation after immigration agents killed two US citizens in Minneapolis in January, calling her leadership “ a disaster ” during the last Senate hearing before her firing.
Tillis was one of a small number of Republicans on Thursday to vote in favor of a Democrat-led war powers resolution that aimed to end the US war with Iran. Despite gaining some Republican support, the proposal failed to pass in the Senate by a 49-50 vote.

As Rihanna said in the clip through laughs, “Wow, baby.”
Another adorable snap sealed the deal that the 12-month-old is following in her mom’s beauty-loving footsteps as she was seen wearing pink hair curlers. Meanwhile, separate footage showed a glammed up Rocki playing with a product from her mom’s Fenty beauty line.

And after the Grammy winner took the bag from her daughter—who was dressed in a tan onesie—she had four five seconds to hand the goods back over as Rocki began to cry, only to be soothed after the designer duds were back in her possession.
Other adorable moments in the carousel included a video of a newborn Rocki cuddling up to her mom, a clip of Rihanna trying to get her baby girl to say “mama,” and a snap of the toddler lounging in a bikini.
And the “Umbrella” singer knows her youngest child is a whole vibe. As she captioned the post, “Who let me have a daughter, bro?”
Recently, Rihanna—also mom to sons RZA , 4, and Riot , 3, with A$AP Rocky—shared another set of rare family photos, this time in her native Barbados.
"One minute I feel like that kid from Westbury," the 38-year-old captioned the photo featuring her three little ones posing in front of her childhood home, shared to Instagram Aug. 11. "The next minute I’m bringing my own kids back to 'Rihanna Drive.'"
The cultural landmark, established in 2017, allows fans to visit the colorful building that Rihanna (born Robyn Rihanna Fenty ) grew up in within the suburbs of Bridgetown.
"Trippy how life works!" the Anti artist continued. "And the Glory STILL and WILL ALWAYS belong to the Almighty Creator!!!"
Since welcoming her three kids, Rihanna has been candid about how motherhood has changed her.
“I’m actually afraid of s--t,” she told Interview Magazine in 2024. “The well-being of your kids, you worry about that constantly. Nobody warns you that having kids means you’re going to worry every second of your life.”
But it’s all worth it if it means being RZA, Riot and Rocki’s mom.
"They bring purpose to every aspect of my life," she told E! News that same year. "Everything has to be intentional, and everything has to be worth it—especially when it takes me away from them."

President Trump invited lefty Mayor Zohran Mamdani to visit him at the White House to “see how I work” after a meeting at Gracie Mansion Monday , a lip reader revealed.
“What I will say, we’ll look after you, but as I say, you’re doing great ,” Trump said, expert lip reader Jeremy Freeman told The Post.
“I’ll look after you, you look after the New Yorkers,” the president said. “And we can both make it work. I wanna support you, help me. Come with me to the White House – see how I work.”
The 90-minute meeting focused on immigration and a Queens housing project for which Mamdani is seeking federal help, with Trump also sharing memories of Gracie Mansion.
It was the first presidential visit to the mayor’s official residence since Ronald Reagan visited Ed Koch in 1981 to tout federal investments in a local roadway project.
The Sunnyside Yards affordable housing project was revived by Mamdani earlier this year after lying dormant for decades — but it needs an infusion of federal dollars to help get it done.
“We appreciate the president’s commitment to the city,” Mamdani told reporters at a briefing after the meeting. “And today, you know, the president shared many of his memories of having been to Gracie Mansion before, having been out here, as well on the lawn. And we appreciated the conversation of how we can work together to deliver a lower cost of living for New Yorkers.”
The socialist mayor and the president, a conservative Republican, struck up an unusual friendship after a White House meeting in February , with Trump telling reporters, “I think he’s a nice guy.”
Mamdani later called the encounter “a productive meeting.”
“I’m looking forward to building more housing in New York City,” the mayor said after the February Oval Office meeting in a post on X, that also included a doctored pic showing Trump holding two copies of the New York Daily News.
One shows the real 1975 headline, “Ford to City: Drop Dead,” and the other a mocked-up version: ‘Trump to City: Let’s Build.”
The chummy chat was at odds with an initial exchange of barbs that saw Mamdani refer to Trump as a “fascist” and a “despot,” while the president referred to the mayor as a communist.
But following Monday’s Big Apple reunion, Trump again had kind words for Mamdani.
“I’ve seen it with numerous different mayors, and I said some great ones and some not so great ones,” he told Mamdani in front of reporters.
“So, hopefully you’re going to be a great one. I’ll be able to say you’re going to be a great one, and you’re off to a good start.”
Trump’s stopover at Gracie Mansion came with the president’s scheduled speech before the UN General Assembly.
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment Tuesday.

articles.title_orig: Bill Gates says an AI ‘kill switch’ isn’t enough
articles.title_zh: Bill Gates says an AI ‘kill switch’ isn’t enough
articles.content_orig:
Microsoft co-founder and philanthropist speaks with NBC’s Kristen Welker in interview airing on Sunday
Bill Gates has called on the US’s federal legislators and law enforcers to regulate the development of artificial intelligence ( AI ), saying in an interview airing on Sunday that the technology left unchecked could cause “a billion deaths” and “no one thinks self-regulation is enough”.
“You need law enforcement and the politicians to get into the discussion about what safeguards and monitoring look like,” the Microsoft co-founder and philanthropist said to Kristen Welker, the NBC Meet the Press host. “And that has to be a required thing.”
Using a term meant to describe an expense required to run a business, Gates continued: “It will be a little bit of overhead for the industry – but not a dramatic slowing of what they’re doing.”
Another portion of the interview – excerpts of which NBC circulated in advance – saw Gates dramatically warn that AI in the wrong hands would be “certainly powerful enough to drive events that, you know, cause a billion deaths”.
“There’s never been a weapon as powerful as the combination of people with ill intent using the latest AI tools,” Gates added, echoing other recent similar warnings by a wide array of tech and political figures.
Gates also addressed the concept of a “kill switch” that could turn off AI if it became too potent, saying it was inadequate.
“It’s not enough to have a kill switch,” Gates remarked. “We’re not yet at the point where … they autonomously grab computers and, you know, can’t be shut down. So that discussion … just sort of shows how non-technical various people are.”
Gates otherwise is generally regarded as optimistic about humans’ future. Many reporting or commenting on his conversation with Welker noted that it occurred in the wake of a nearly 6,000-word essay that he published in late August warning about AI and the potentially lethal ills it poses to humanity on a large scale.
His fellow tech moguls including Sam Altman and Elon Musk have joined Gates in calling for a slowdown of the development of AI, which some experts theorize could precipitate the mass destruction of humans through bioweapons and nuclear war, among other methods.
Progressive US senator Bernie Sanders on 23 September proposed legislation that would temporarily pause advanced AI development while guardrails to the technology are put in place.
Meanwhile, Microsoft itself has been challenged for having a role in stoking some of the dystopian concerns surrounding AI.
Company employees and activists have organized a campaign aimed at getting Microsoft to cut ties with the Israeli military, which has used AI tools to kill in Gaza and – alongside US forces – in Iran, according to a Guardian essay published on Friday.
The essay’s authors, Mohamed Hussein and Granate Kim of the No Azure for Apartheid group, furthermore warned that “horrors wrought by AI” are also being seen in the US. For instance, the US Department of Homeland Security has used AI tools such as Microsoft’s Azure to monitor, arrest and deport immigrants en masse, Hussein and Kim wrote.
Gates’s essay in August and interview on Sunday were two of his first major forays into the public since becoming ensnared in the scandal surrounding Jeffrey Epstein, the disgraced financier who pleaded guilty in 2008 to procuring a minor for prostitution before dying by suicide while incarcerated on sex-trafficking charges 11 years later.
An external review commissioned by Gates’s philanthropic foundation and released in July determined that he was among a number of organization staffers and leaders who had collectively held about 30 meetings with Epstein from 2011 to 2014.
Gates has not been accused of involvement in Epstein’s admitted or alleged crimes. He has said he regretted “every minute” he spent with Epstein, and remains the chair of the $89bn (£65bn) Gates Foundation charity.
In a lighter moment during Welker’s interview with Gates, the host asked him: “Are there any ways in which you, professionally or personally, avoid AI and say that: ‘I’m not going to consult with it in this instance?’”
Gates, with a chuckle and a smile, replied: “Well, I’m not using it for my personal relationships. I’m not like: ‘Hey, do you like me? Hey, am I a nice guy?’
“So I just never went down that path, because I’m lucky in terms of my family, friends and everything. I don’t socialize with the AI. It knows I’m a very serious person.”

Security researcher Rowan Howard-Jones says that OpenAI agents scanned the UN Conference on Trade and Development’s (UNCTAD) statistics site over 16,000 times between April and June . While the incident doesn’t quite rise to the level of the Hugging Face hack , or the recent attacks on US government sites , it’s yet another concerning example of AI agents going outside the normal bounds to accomplish a task.
According to Howard-Jones, the agents were likely tasked with retrieving publicly available data related to the Productive Capacities Index (PCI) through the UNCTADstat API. However, the agents did not appear to have direct API access and were limited in their ability to pull data from UNCTADstat because of restrictions on their HTTP tools.
The agents eventually worked out a way to bypass their limitations and start pulling data from the site, but still encountered some errors. At this point, the AI went from creative to deceptive. Believing that the errors were due to its requests being caught by a nonexistent filter, it started to mask its behavior. It eventually realized it could hijack Google’s XSS game (a cross-site scripting learning tool) to accomplish its goals. The agents resorted to increasingly aggressive tactics to get access to UN data.
OpenAI and the UN did not immediately reply to a request for comment.
